stories.headline: After Kulgam terror attack, Farooq Abdullah advocates "path of dialogue" with Pakistan
stories.title: After Kulgam terror attack, Farooq Abdullah advocates "path of dialogue" with Pakistan
stories.summary: Srinagar, Nov 12 : Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Farooq Abdullah on Thursday called on Pakistan to end terrorism and choose dialogue to resolve outstanding issues, amid a spate of security incidents in Jammu and Kashmir, including the killing of two Special Police Officers (SPOs) in Kishtwar. Abdullah said terrorism should not intimidate people and reiterated that Kashmir was, is and will always remain a part of India. He also emphasised the need to revive the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) to facilitate dialogue and regional cooperation. "Terrorism exists, but we must not be intimidated by it. Kashmir was, is, and will always remain a part of India... I have always told Pakistan: put an end to terrorism. Terrorism will lead nowhere. Choose the path of dialogue; that is the only way a solution can be found. We were once part of the same nation... We must revive SAARC so that we can all sit together, resolve our issues, and move toward progress," he said. Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) MLA Aga Syed Muntazir Mehdi strongly condemned the attack on CRPF personnel in Kulgam on Wednesday and the killing of two SPOs in Kishtwar, while questioning the Central Government's approach towards Kashmir. He said violence had no place in a civilised or democratic society and stressed that controlling the visible signs of instability could not be considered a permanent solution. "We strongly condemn yesterday’s attack in Kulgam and the incident reported in Kishtwar today. Violence has no place in a civilised or democratic society. However, these repeated incidents raise serious questions about the Central Government’s approach towards Kashmir... The government may have controlled the visible signs of instability, but control is not a permanent solution," Mehdi said. In Kulgam district, a massive cordon and search operation (CASO) continued on Thursday after unidentified motorcycle-borne assailants opened fire on CRPF personnel deployed at a security checkpoint in Nowpora Akhran on Wednesday. The attack took place at around 2:15 pm, when the assailants opened fire on the security personnel before fleeing the spot. Three CRPF personnel sustained injuries in the firing and were shifted to a hospital in Anantnag district for treatment. In another incident from Kishtwar, the bullet-riddled bodies of the two SPOs, identified as Babi Chand (57) and Rashpal Kumar (45), were recovered on Thursday morning, a day after they went missing in the remote Dachhan belt. The two personnel were posted with the Special Operations Group (SOG) of the local police at Kiyar village in Dachhan. They had gone missing on Wednesday while travelling from their camp towards an Army post at Dharna-Marwah. Kishtwar MLA Shagun Parihar expressed grief over the killings, stating that the bodies of the two personnel were recovered at around 8 am and 9 am, respectively. "Regarding the incident in which two SPOs (Special Police Officers) were reportedly killed—what are your thoughts? It is a truly tragic incident. Two of our SPOs from the southern region have been killed. They had gone missing last night, and their bodies were recovered this morning—one around 8:00 AM and the other around 9:00 AM. It is deeply saddening," Parihar said. (ANI)

stories.title: Sikkim: 4.9-Magnitude Earthquake Strikes Near Nepal Border, Tremors Felt in Gangtok
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: An earthquake measuring 4.9 on the Richter scale struck the Sikkim-Nepal region early on 12th November’s morning,, triggering tremors across parts of West and East Sikkim, including the state capital, Gangtok.
As per official there were no immediate reports of casualtiesor damage to property.
As per the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at around 4.30 am, with its epicentre located approximately 40 km north-west of Yuksom in Gyalshing district of West Sikkim.
The tremor was recorded at a depth of 73 km, at latitude 27.671 degrees north and longitude 87.987 degrees east.
People residing in several areas of West Sikkim and parts of East Sikkim, including Gangtok, reported experiencing mild tremors following the earthquake.
The early-morning tremor caused panic like situation among people, although no immediate reports of injuries or structural damage had emerged at the time of filing this report.

stories.headline: India’s GDP growth seen at 7.7% in Q3 on strong manufacturing push
stories.title: India’s GDP growth seen at 7.7% in Q3 on strong manufacturing push
stories.summary: India’s economy is expected to remain robust in Q3 FY27, with GDP growth projected at 7.7% and GVA growth at 8.1%, driven by strong manufacturing, industrial activity, consumer demand and credit growth, despite global uncertainties and potential risks from oil prices and geopolitics.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s economy is expected to remain robust in Q3 FY27, with GDP growth projected at 7.7% and GVA growth at 8.1%, driven by strong manufacturing, industrial activity, consumer demand and credit growth, despite global uncertainties and potential risks from oil prices and geopolitics.

New Delhi: India’s GDP growth remains strong and is expected to reach 7.7 per cent year-on-year in the October-November period (Q3), with GVA growth estimated at 8.1 per cent, a report by BofA Global Research said on Thursday.
BofA maintains its full-year FY27 GDP growth forecast at 7.4 per cent, with modest upside risks, projecting 7.5 per cent growth for FY28.
The growth reflects resilient economic momentum despite global supply-side headwinds from the West Asia disruption, uneven monsoons, and weakness in the farm sector.
Strong industrial and manufacturing activity, along with sustained consumer demand and credit growth, is expected to support overall growth.
Manufacturing is expected to grow around 12 per cent, supported by stronger industrial activity, with IIP growth rising to 7.3 per cent in Q3 from 6.2 per cent in Q2, the report showed.
Auto sales, power demand, and freight activity remain strong, while bank credit growth continues at around 20 per cent.
“We expect the H1 FY27 GDP growth to now average at 7.7 per cent YoY, modestly lower than 8.1 per cent YoY in H2 FY26.
We continue to project GDP growth for the full year at 7.4 per cent YoY for FY27 but see modest upside risks to our GDP growth projections,” said the report.
The nominal GDP growth estimate for Q2 FY27 is around 13.9 per cent YoY, which will be the highest nominal growth print in almost four years.
“We expect the growth momentum to hold in the next fiscal year and keep our forecast unchanged for FY28 at 7.5 per cent YoY.
The growth momentum in India appears quite resilient, however, the downside risks to activity appear largely global in nature.

stories.headline: India bonds to stay hemmed in by oil, Treasury moves ahead of inflation data
stories.title: India bonds to stay hemmed in by oil, Treasury moves ahead of inflation data
stories.summary: The 10-year US Treasury yield neared 5% as hot October inflation data boosted bets on a larger Fed rate hike in December
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Indian government bonds are likely to trade in a narrow range on Thursday, wedged between softer oil prices and rising US yields, while investors await domestic inflation data that could reshape expectations for the Reserve Bank of India’s rate path.

The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield neared 5% in Asian trade after October consumer-price data outstripped forecasts, spurring traders to ramp up bets on a larger Federal Reserve rate increase in December.
Markets await India’s October inflation reading later in the day, with a Reuters poll forecasting annual consumer inflation at 5.93%, up from 5.54% in September.
An upside surprise could entrench expectations of further RBI tightening next month.
Softer crude may provide some relief.
Brent fell 1% in Asian trade to $91.80 a barrel, easing pressure on oil-importing India’s inflation outlook, currency and public finances.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to move between 7.18% and 7.23%, according to a private-bank trader.
It ended at 7.2139% on Wednesday after rising 6 basis points, its steepest single-day climb in a month.
Volumes were thin on Wednesday as investors stayed on the sidelines ahead of Friday’s 340-billion-rupee auction of the benchmark 10-year bond, a hefty supply test that could gauge investor appetite.
“The best time to take positions would be after Friday’s auction, once uncertainty around CPI, the RBI’s rate path and investor appetite has cleared,” an asset-manager trader said.
The RBI, which raised its key rate in October for the first time in nearly four years, is expected to deliver another 25 bps of tightening in December.
Some traders are also positioning for a 50-bp increase.

stories.headline: Tata Power Appoints Sanjay Banga as CEO and Managing Director
stories.title: Tata Power Appoints Sanjay Banga as CEO and Managing Director
stories.summary: Tata Power, at its latest Board meeting, appointed Sanjay Banga as Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Managing Director (MD), and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP) for a five-year term from May 1, 2027, to April 30, 2032 (both days inclusive), subject to shareholder approval. Effective November 11, 2026, Banga has also been appointed as an Additional Director of Tata Power and Chief Executive Officer Designate (CEO) of the company. In a regulatory filing, Tata Power announced Sanjay Banga's appointment , following the Board of Directors' decision based on the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee. Previously, Banga served as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Managing Director (MD) of Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited. He currently serves as President – Renewables at The Tata Power Company Limited (Tata Power). Banga is a power-sector professional with more than three decades of experience in the operational and commercial management of distribution companies, business development, digital transformation, project management, change management, regulatory advocacy and stakeholder management. Brief Profile Banga previously served as President of the Transmission and Distribution businesses. His responsibilities included overseeing the performance of distribution companies across Odisha, Mumbai, Delhi and Ajmer. He was also responsible for overseeing Mumbai's transmission business, Powerlinks Transmission Limited and transmission assets in Uttar Pradesh. Banga also served as the Chief Executive Officer of Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (TPDDL), a notable public-private partnership (JV) between Tata Power and the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi. Banga began his career as an Engineer Trainee at National Thermal Power Corporation Limited (NTPC), where he was involved in the operation and commissioning of super thermal power projects from 1989 to 1995. Before joining TPDDL in 2003, he worked with Reliance Energy (formerly BSES Limited) from 1996 to 2003. His responsibilities covered operations, maintenance, planning, design and project engineering for thermal power projects. His experience with public- and private-sector electricity utilities in India has given him a broad understanding of the challenges facing the electricity distribution sector. He is also a regular speaker at seminars, workshops and panel discussions in India and abroad. Banga is an alumnus of the National Institute of Technology, Kurukshetra, and holds a Master of Business Administration degree from the Faculty of Management Studies, University of Delhi. He has also completed the Senior Executive Leadership Program at Harvard Business School and holds alumni status.

Case Title: SAINABA VERSUS STATE OF KERALA & ANR.

The Supreme Court held that a statutory demand notice under the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 cannot be treated as invalid merely because it was received by a family member of the drawer, when the notice was dispatched by registered post to the drawer's correct address.

A bench of Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah and Justice Manmohan set aside the Kerala High Court's judgment, which had overturned the drawer's conviction solely on the ground that the statutory demand notice was not received by him personally but by his mother, who resided at the address provided by the drawer.

The Court said that once a demand notice is dispatched by registered post to the correct address, a rebuttable presumption of service arises shifting the burden upon the drawer to rebut the presumption by establishing, for instance, that the address was incorrect, that he had no knowledge of the notice, or that the postal endorsement was incorrect.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday (September 30) held that, under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the Adjudicating Authority can recall the admission of a Section 9 insolvency application if the proceedings were initiated based on fraudulent or collusive jurisdictional facts.
However, the Court clarified that such a finding of fraud does not automatically require termination of the entire Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP).

Once insolvency proceedings have been admitted and have assumed an in rem character, the Adjudicating Authority (AA) must separately determine whether the CIRP should continue in the interests of the corporate debtor and its other stakeholders.

stories.headline: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.title: Technological superiority key to enhancing operational readiness against emerging threats: Rajanth Singh
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 12: Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has called upon the Defence Forces to strengthen and sustain both offensive and defensive dimensions of the ‘element of surprise’ to maintain operational readiness against conventional and emerging threats arising from rapid technological advancements and the evolving nature of modern warfare. Addressing the Air Force Commanders’ Conference in New Delhi on November 12, 2026, he emphasised the need to continue bolstering intelligence and surveillance capabilities, enhance integration among systems and identify potential threats before they unfold. “Our Defence Forces must develop capabilities and methods that leave the adversary with no time to react or recover, while simultaneously ensuring that we are never caught off guard by an unexpected move from the enemy. Surprise can manifest in various forms, both conventional and electronic. Our intelligence and surveillance mechanisms must be further strengthened and operational preparedness enhanced to ensure that our personnel remain alert, agile and equipped to respond effectively to any emerging challenge,” said the Raksha Mantri. Shri Rajnath Singh asserted that contemporary conflicts are extending beyond traditional battlefields into non-contact domains, with missiles, drones and advanced weapon systems playing a significant role. Referring to the Russia-Ukraine and Israel-Hamas conflicts, he stated that drones and air defence systems have emerged as critical components of modern warfare. He exhorted the Commanders to remain prepared for emerging challenges such as kamikaze drones, surveillance and counter-drone operations. Raksha Mantri called upon the Indian Air Force (IAF) to develop dedicated doctrines and architectures for emerging domains of warfare, including electronic, cyber and space.
